title: Ignore generated files
summary: A .gitignore file lists patterns Git should ignore when files are not already tracked. It is useful for temporary output.
introduction: A .gitignore file lists patterns Git should ignore when files are not already tracked. It is useful for temporary output. We will use a small example so you can follow each step.
learningObjectives: Use the example to answer a practice question

blocks.text: A .gitignore file lists patterns Git should ignore when files are not already tracked. It is useful for temporary output.
The untracked scratch.log is ignored. The .gitignore file itself can be tracked.

items: Read the example from top to bottom. Point to the part that uses the new idea.
Add a second temporary file pattern.
Explain what changed in your own words. Check the example again if you get stuck.

blocks.title: A common mistake
blocks.text: Ignoring a file does not remove it from earlier commits or erase a leaked secret.
For more detail later, use this [Git further reading](https://git-scm.com/docs/gittutorial).
